..
Issued at 403 AM EST Mon Nov 2 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

Ridging builds across the center of the country as sharp troughing 
plows into the western US. Abundant difluence over the Central 
Plains attm ahead of the base of the trough as PV maxima lifts 
across the Four Corners region into the lee of the Rockies. Strong 
southwesterly mid-level jet resulting in abundant Pacific moisture 
transport into the CONUS...with extremely anomalous pwats in the 
realm of 6-7 standard deviations above climo norms streaming into 
the Central Plains. Increasing southerly flow through the length of 
the Plains (40+kt LLJ) resulting in anomalous moisture wrapping over 
the ridge axis into southern Ontario, albeit to less extremes than 
out west (pwats generally running 2-4 standard deviations above the 
mean...which is still notable). 850mb temps rise into the teens 
again across the southern and central Plains...with the cold air 
slipping by well to our northeast over Quebec with troughing up 
there; cold front along the edge of this cold air drapes across 
Hudson Bay. 1033mb surface high over the Mid-Atlantic; with surface 
pressure falls congealing into a broad area of sub-1004mb over the 
eastern Rockies into the western Plains. A couple longitudinal cold 
fronts present with this system, through CO and NM ahead of the 
trough axis, and stretching from AZ northwestward into WY, with a 
stationary boundary stretching from here into southern Manitoba. 
Here in the Great Lakes...a warm day yesterday with overnight temps 
attm near or slightly warmer than last night; some semblance of 
warm/moist advection resulting in a little more fog/low-clouds 
around tonight, particularly across the EUP and Tip of the Mitt, 
downwind of Lake MI and also where more favorable moisture lingered 
all day.

Trough axis will continue to track eastward across the central CONUS 
today through midweek, driving surface pressure falls across the 
Upper Midwest through this period. Amid a very anomalously moist 
environment, expect heavy rain concerns across the Plains/Upper 
Midwest, with less certainty with eastward extent, which should be 
further away from the more robust synoptic forcing with this system. 
Upper trough may attempt to close off Tuesday into Wednesday before 
additional upstream energy kicks it eastward for the latter half of 
the week, dragging the trough axis across the area and bringing a 
little cooler air back into the region for the end of the week. 
Another wad of PV will punch its way across the northern CONUS later 
this week, with signals for troughing to try to settle into the 
eastern US again going into next weekend...though the evolution of 
this remains unclear. 

FORECAST DETAILS...

Rain tonight into Tuesday (likely beyond as well)...think widespread 
rain could move in as soon as late afternoon for our Lake MI zones, 
but should begin to overspread the area after 0z, with chances 
lasting through the night, right on into Tuesday. Think the deepest 
moisture will lift northward through the area Tuesday morning, 
resulting in potential for a break in the more widespread rain...but 
given a stout saturated layer in the low/mid-levels, would not be 
surprised if we ended up with some drizzle around. The better 
forcing appears to remain to our north and likely just to our west 
tonight into Tuesday morning, and therefore, not surprised the EUP 
has been removed from the excessive rain outlook since yesterday 
morning's forecast discussion. Even so...some signals in 
deterministic guidance (increasingly in hi-res guidance as well) 
suggest a period of heavy rain will be possible across the 
central/EUP overnight...with as much as 0.50-1in of rainfall in 6hrs 
ending 12z Tuesday, which is much more than the current rainfall 
forecast suggests, though I have tweaked it up a tiny bit for now, 
in the realm of 0.30+in for that 6hr period, given the anomalously 
moist environment that will be present (pwats increasing to or above 
1.5in) and signals for a theta-e advection maximum across the Yoop 
tonight; any localized forcing could certainly squeeze out quite a 
bit of moisture (incoming warm nose may also be a little more 
supportive of efficient rainfall production as well). Given drought 
conditions across the bulk of the UP attm, think an inch or so of 
rain will be helpful...do worry a bit about some hydro impacts up 
there if it all comes at once, noting some of our rivers are a bit 
flashy north of the Bridge.  

Heaviest rainfall concerns should be tonight into Tuesday with this 
initial surge of warm advection ahead of the strengthening system 
upstream. Showery activity could hang out as the upper low slowly 
meanders eastward through the middle of the week. There appears to 
be another shot of rain with cold advection as the trough axis 
finally exits the region Thursday. This latter period has potential 
to support overlake instability as 850mb temps fall to or below 0C 
again going into Thursd
